facts.object: Mr. Doyle attended for scheduled review. He reported stable exertional dyspnea at two flights of stairs and no orthopnea. Examination: BP 148/86, heart rate 74 regular, mild ankle edema, lungs clear. Laboratory results (LD-03): HbA1c 8.1%, creatinine 142 umol/L (eGFR 49 mL/min/1.73 m2, stage G3a at that time), potassium 4.7 mmol/L. Plan: refer to cardiology for echocardiography; continue metformin 1,000 mg twice daily (eGFR at that date was above the PRO-008 cap threshold of 45); repeat labs in 6 months.

facts.object: On 2025-02-20 creatinine was 158 umol/L, eGFR 44. Under PRO-008 (see HO-02), metformin is capped at 1,000 mg/day when eGFR is 30 to 44 (FPA-03). The PharmaSafe system generated a renal-dose advisory, but it was filed in the pharmacist work queue rather than the prescriber inbox. The dose therefore remained 2,000 mg/day for **21 days** until the pharmacist telephone review of 2025-03-13 (ENC-001-08), when the dose was reduced to 500 mg twice daily and the patient was counseled on sick-day rules. At ENC-001-09 (2025-05-14), eGFR 43 with metformin 1,000 mg/day was compliant. Metformin would be stopped if eGFR fell below 30; it has not.

The dose therefore remained 2,000 mg/day for **21 days** until the pharmacist telephone review of 2025-03-13 (ENC-001-08), when the dose was reduced to 500 mg twice daily and the patient was counseled on sick-day rules. At ENC-001-09 (2025-05-14), eGFR 43 with metformin 1,000 mg/day was compliant. Metformin would be stopped if eGFR fell below 30; it has not.

facts.object: At discharge on 2025-03-07 the cardiology team **stopped aspirin and continued apixaban 5 mg twice daily with clopidogrel 75 mg daily**. The recorded rationale was: (1) DG-01 limits aspirin in patients with atrial fibrillation who need an anticoagulant to a peri-procedural course of no more than 7 days; aspirin had been given for 5 days; (2) the bleeding-risk score on the DG-01 rubric was 3 (age over 65, low body weight, hypertension), indicating elevated risk; (3) PRO-007 (HO-04) requires pharmacist review of any combination containing an anticoagulant and an antiplatelet, which was completed on 2025-03-06. The apixaban dose-reduction criteria in MP-03 were reviewed: only one of the three criteria was present (weight 58 kg; age under 80; creatinine 0.9 mg/dL with eGFR 72), so the full dose was kept. Clopidogrel was planned for six months to 2025-09-04.

Stewardship (DEP-007, PRO-013) reviewed the course and accepted 5 days because symptoms had resolved and the interaction harm outweighed further benefit; a repeat urine culture on 2025-11-04 was negative. Warfarin was held on 2025-10-26 and 2025-10-27. INR was 4.1 on 2025-10-27, 3.2 on 2025-10-28, and 2.6 on 2025-10-29. Warfarin resumed on 2025-10-28 at 4 mg daily. Hemoglobin on 2025-10-26 was 12.9 g/dL; there was no major bleeding. The anticoagulation rule that an INR above 4.5 triggers a clinic call within 24 hours (FPA-05) was **met**. The overridden alert, with no INR plan, was reported as **INC-003** and reviewed in HO-08. Warfarin was completed on 2025-11-29 (about 3 months from 2025-08-29).

facts.object: DG-01 recommends a renin-angiotensin system blocker after ACS when LVEF is below 50% or hypertension persists. Compare PAT-001 (PR-01), who takes lisinopril without any allergy flag.
